projects.name: Analytics Dashboard
projects.description:
A new analytics dashboard platform that combines three data domains: (1) customer CSV file ingestion and processing, (2) application log analysis, and (3) interactive visualization components. The goal is a single dashboard where business users can explore customer metrics and engineering teams can monitor application log insights, backed by a shared processing and storage layer.

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-pipeline, csv, logs, visualization

tasks.name: M1: Foundation, Architecture & Project Scaffolding
tasks.details:
Milestone goal: establish the technical foundation all three data domains depend on so CSV processing, log analysis, and visualization teams build against one shared contract.

Deliverables:
- Agreed tech stack and repository structure (frontend, backend/API, processing workers, infra)
- Shared data model and schemas for customer records, log events, and dashboard metrics
- Local development environment and CI skeleton
- Storage layer decision (warehouse + object storage for raw CSV/log files)

Exit criteria: a new developer can clone, run the stack locally, and run a passing CI pipeline. Data schemas reviewed and signed off by both business and engineering stakeholders.

tasks.name: M2: Customer CSV Data Processing Pipeline
tasks.details:
Milestone goal: reliably turn messy customer CSV exports into clean, queryable, deduplicated customer records that the dashboard can visualize.

Scope:
- CSV upload/ingest path (manual upload + scheduled pull from source location)
- Parsing, schema/type validation, and row-level error reporting
- Cleaning and normalization (dedupe, null handling, field mapping, encoding issues)
- Loading into the analytics store with idempotent, re-runnable jobs
- Observability on pipeline runs (row counts, rejects, duration)

Exit criteria: a real customer CSV of ~1M rows processes end-to-end with a visible, actionable error report and data lands in the analytics store. Blocked-by: M1.

tasks.name: M3: Application Log Analysis Pipeline
tasks.details:
Milestone goal: ingest application logs and turn them into searchable events plus pre-aggregated error/latency metrics the dashboard can chart.

Scope:
- Log ingestion (file/batch shipping, rotation-aware, retention policy)
- Parsing into structured events (timestamp, level, service, request id, message, stack trace)
- Aggregations: error rates by service/time, p50/p95/p99 latency, top error signatures
- Log search/query API with time-range and service filters
- Anomaly/threshold flagging for spike detection

Exit criteria: a week of real application logs is ingested and queryable, with error-rate and latency aggregates matching a manual spot check. Blocked-by: M1.

tasks.name: M4: Visualization Components & Dashboard Experience
tasks.details:
Milestone goal: deliver the user-facing dashboard composed of reusable, individually testable visualization components consuming the metrics APIs from M2 and M3.

Scope:
- Dashboard shell: layout, routing, navigation, responsive grid
- Reusable chart component library (time series, bar, KPI card, table, distribution)
- Customer analytics views (cohort/segment breakdowns, retention-style views)
- Log analytics views (error timeline, latency percentiles, top error signatures)
- Global filters (date range, segment, service) with shared state and URL persistence
- Loading, empty, and error states; accessibility basics

Exit criteria: stakeholders can complete the two core user journeys (customer metrics review, log troubleshooting) in a staging dashboard without help. Blocked-by: M1; data-dependent views unblocked incrementally as M2/M3 land.

tasks.name: M5: Integration, Testing, Security & Launch
tasks.details:
Milestone goal: prove the three domains work together under realistic load, is secure and monitored, and ship it.

Scope:
- End-to-end integration of pipelines -> API -> dashboard
- Test strategy: unit, integration, pipeline data-quality tests, E2E on core journeys
- Performance/load validation and query tuning on dashboard-critical queries
- Auth, role-based access, secrets handling, PII review for customer data and logs
- Monitoring, alerting, runbooks, and on-call handover
- Phased rollout plan and launch checklist

Exit criteria: load test at target concurrency passes SLOs, security review signed off, runbooks published, and the dashboard is live for the pilot user group. Blocked-by: M2, M3, M4.

tasks.name: 1.1 Choose tech stack and define repository structure
tasks.details:
Pick the languages/frameworks for frontend, backend API, and batch/stream processing; decide monorepo vs polyrepo and lay out top-level folders.

Acceptance criteria:
- One-page decision record listing stack choices and rejected alternatives
- Repository skeleton created with README explaining each top-level directory
- Team walkthrough completed (30 min) and questions captured

Explicitly out of scope: installing any dependencies or writing application code.

tasks.name: 1.2 Design customer record schema and log event schema
tasks.details:
Define the canonical target schemas both pipelines will write to.

In scope:
- customer_records: identity keys, segment attributes, lifecycle dates, source lineage, PII flags
- log_events: timestamp, level, service, request_id, message, stack_trace, latency_ms, host
- Metric/DTO shapes consumed by the visualization layer
- Naming conventions, units, timezone policy (UTC), and null semantics

Acceptance criteria:
- Schema definitions checked into the repo as versioned files
- Sample rows documented for each entity
- Business stakeholder sign-off on customer fields; engineering sign-off on log fields

Split this task further if schema review surfaces any entity needing more than one owner.

tasks.name: 1.3 Provision analytics warehouse and object storage
tasks.details:
Stand up the storage layer: an analytics warehouse/schema for queryable tables and an object store bucket for raw CSV and log archives.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dev and staging instances created with names/tags matching repo conventions
- Raw-upload bucket created with lifecycle/retention rule placeholder
- Service credentials issued and stored in the team secret manager (not in the repo)
- Connectivity verified from a laptop and from CI

Note: production provisioning is deferred to M5 launch prep; this covers dev + staging only.

tasks.name: 1.4 Build local development environment (one-command startup)
tasks.details:
Provide a single documented command that brings up the API, a local warehouse, the object store, and the frontend dev server.

Acceptance criteria:
- `make dev` (or equivalent) starts all services from a clean clone
- .env.example committed with every required variable documented
- README quickstart verified by one engineer who has never run the project
- Local seed data script exists for both customer and log samples

Keep seed data to a handful of fabricated rows; real data is never committed.

tasks.name: 1.5 Set up CI pipeline (lint, test, build)
tasks.details:
Create the continuous integration skeleton that all later tasks depend on.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI runs on every pull request: linters, unit tests, and a build of both API and frontend
- Failing checks block merge on the main branch
- Pipeline runtime under 10 minutes on a small change
- Status badge added to README

Thresholds/coverage gates are intentionally not enforced yet; that is part of task 5.2.

tasks.name: 1.6 Scaffold API service and publish interface contract
tasks.details:
Create the backend service skeleton that both pipelines feed and the dashboard consumes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Health-check endpoint deployed in dev and returning version info
- OpenAPI (or equivalent) spec stub listing planned endpoints for customer metrics and log metrics
- Error response format standardized (code, message, details)
- Auth middleware placeholder wired in behind a feature flag

Endpoint implementations belong to M2/M3; this task delivers only the skeleton and the contract.

tasks.name: 2.1 Build CSV upload endpoint with file-level validation
tasks.details:
Accept a customer CSV upload, store the raw file in object storage, and enqueue a processing job.

Acceptance criteria:
- Accepts multipart upload up to an agreed size limit (default 500 MB), streams to object storage rather than buffering fully in memory
- Rejects non-CSV content types and files missing required headers with a clear 4xx message
- Writes a raw-file record (filename, size, checksum, uploader, timestamp) and returns a job id
- Duplicate upload detected by checksum and reported rather than silently reprocessed

Deliberately excludes row-level validation, which is task 2.3.

tasks.name: 2.2 Implement CSV parser with encoding and delimiter detection
tasks.details:
Turn raw bytes into records reliably, given that customer exports vary in encoding and formatting.

Acceptance criteria:
- Detects UTF-8, UTF-8 with BOM, and Latin-1; falls back gracefully with a logged warning
- Auto-detects comma vs semicolon vs tab delimiters and quoted fields containing delimiters/newlines
- Handles embedded newlines in quoted address fields without splitting rows
- Streams in chunks so a 1M-row file stays within a fixed memory budget
- Unit tests cover each encoding, delimiter, and quoting case

Performance tuning beyond the memory budget is out of scope here and handled in 5.4.

tasks.name: 2.3 Add schema validation and row-level error reporting
tasks.details:
Validate each parsed row against the customer schema and produce an actionable reject report.

Acceptance criteria:
- Per-field type, format, and required checks (dates, emails, currency, country codes)
- Rejected rows are captured with row number, field, offending value, and reason
- Job summary exposes total / accepted / rejected counts
- Reject report downloadable as CSV; capped sample shown in the UI response
- Configurable policy: fail the whole job above an error threshold, otherwise partial-load

Deciding the customer-visible threshold wording with business stakeholders is part of this task.

tasks.name: 2.4 Implement normalization and deduplication rules
tasks.details:
Convert accepted rows into canonical customer records and collapse duplicates.

Acceptance criteria:
- Field mapping config from source headers to canonical schema fields, editable without code changes
- Normalizes casing, whitespace, phone/country codes, and currency to base units
- Deterministic dedupe key defined (e.g. normalized email + customer id) with documented tie-break rule for "most recent wins"
- Merge conflicts written to a reviewable audit table rather than dropped silently
- Agreed null/unknown handling documented per field

This task does not load data; persistence is task 2.5.

tasks.name: 2.5 Load customer records into analytics store idempotently
tasks.details:
Persist normalized records into the warehouse using an upsert pattern.

Acceptance criteria:
- Re-running the same file produces identical row counts and no duplicate customers
- Upsert keyed on canonical customer id; soft-delete flag for records absent from a full refresh
- Load performed in batches with transactional per-batch commits
- Row-count reconciliation between accepted rows and target table logged at job end
- Backfill path documented for re-processing a historical file

Index/tuning work is deferred to 5.4.

tasks.name: 2.6 Schedule automated pull from the customer file source
tasks.details:
Move from manual upload to a recurring pull of new customer exports from the agreed source (SFTP or shared bucket).

Acceptance criteria:
- Cron/scheduler entry runs on the agreed cadence with timezone documented
- Only new or changed files picked up (tracked by filename + checksum manifest)
- Failure sends an alert and retries with bounded backoff
- Dry-run mode available so the schedule can be tested without loading data

Credentials for the source location must come from the secret manager, never config files.

tasks.name: 2.7 Add pipeline observability: run metrics and failure alerts
tasks.details:
Make CSV pipeline health visible without reading logs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each run emits duration, input rows, accepted, rejected, loaded counts
- Dashboard-ready run-history table queryable by date and source file
- Alert fires on any failed run or on a success-rate drop below an agreed threshold
- Structured logs include job id and file checksum for traceability

Full runbook authoring is part of 5.6; this task only covers metrics and alert wiring.

tasks.name: 3.1 Configure log ingestion, rotation handling, and retention
tasks.details:
Get application logs reliably from the running systems into the raw log store.

Acceptance criteria:
- Batch shipping from the agreed log locations (files or agent), covering the pilot services
- Rotation-aware: files renamed/compressed mid-read are not lost or double-counted
- Retention policy set for raw logs (default 30 days) and applied by the storage lifecycle rule
- Ingestion lag metric exposed (time from log write to availability)
- Connection failure retried with bounded backoff

Parsing into structured events is task 3.2 and is out of scope here.

tasks.name: 3.2 Build log parser into structured events
tasks.details:
Convert raw log lines (multiple formats: JSON and plain text) into the canonical log_events schema.

Acceptance criteria:
- Handles at least the two dominant formats in our logs (structured JSON and bracketed text) plus multiline stack traces
- Extracts timestamp (normalized to UTC), level, service, request_id, message, stack_trace, latency_ms, host
- Unparseable lines routed to a dead-letter table with raw text and reason, never silently dropped
- Parser version recorded on each event for re-processing
- Unit tests per format including malformed input

Format-specific quirks for any third format found in discovery become their own follow-up task, not a scope increase here.

tasks.name: 3.3 Build error-rate and latency aggregation jobs
tasks.details:
Produce the pre-aggregated metrics the log dashboard charts, so the UI never scans raw events.

Acceptance criteria:
- Hourly and daily rollups of error count and error rate per service
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) per service and endpoint per time bucket
- Aggregates are incremental and re-runnable for a given time window without double-counting
- Results validated against a manual spot check on one day of real logs
- Aggregate tables documented with grain, dimensions, and refresh cadence

Percentile correctness at very low request volumes must be explicitly documented as a known limitation.

tasks.name: 3.4 Group errors into normalized signatures
tasks.details:
Collapse thousands of distinct error messages into a ranked list of error signatures for the "top errors" panel.

Acceptance criteria:
- Normalization strips volatile parts (ids, timestamps, numbers, host names) before grouping
- Top-N signatures per service and time window with first-seen, last-seen, and occurrence counts
- Representative sample message and one stack trace retained per signature
- Grouping quality reviewed on real logs; obvious over- or under-grouping cases documented
- Signature assignment is stable across runs for the same input

Rendering this in the UI belongs to task 4.5.

tasks.name: 3.5 Expose log search and metrics query API
tasks.details:
Give the dashboard a single, documented API for log events and log metrics.

Acceptance criteria:
- Endpoints: event search (time range, service, level, free-text), metrics rollups, error signatures
- Server-side pagination with a hard result cap and cursor-based navigation
- Response times under the agreed budget for a 7-day range on staging data
- Input validation returns clear errors for inverted time ranges and unknown services
- OpenAPI spec updated and examples committed

Caching, if needed, is evaluated in 5.4 rather than assumed here.

tasks.name: 4.1 Build dashboard shell: layout, routing, navigation
tasks.details:
Create the app frame every view plugs into, with no real data yet.

Acceptance criteria:
- Responsive two-level layout (sidebar sections: Customers, Logs) collapsing correctly at mobile/tablet/desktop widths
- Routing with deep links per view so a view can be shared by URL
- Placeholder pages for each planned view render without errors
- Header shows environment badge (dev/staging/prod) to prevent mistakes
- Component tests for routing and layout breakpoints

Charting and data fetching are explicitly out of scope for this task.

tasks.name: 4.2 Build reusable chart primitives (time series, bar, distribution)
tasks.details:
Create the chart building blocks with a single consistent API, driven by static fixture data.

Acceptance criteria:
- Time series, stacked bar, and distribution/histogram components with a shared prop contract
- Consistent axis, tooltip, legend, and color-token behavior across charts
- Handles sparse data, single-point series, and zero-variance series without breaking
- Charts render from fixture JSON, no live API dependency
- Storybook-style visual catalog (or equivalent) so reviewers can see all variants

Accessibility for charts (keyboard/screen-reader summaries) is task 4.7, not this one.

tasks.name: 4.3 Build KPI card and sortable data table components
tasks.details:
Deliver the two non-chart primitives used on nearly every page.

Acceptance criteria:
- KPI card: value, delta vs previous period, trend direction, optional sparkline, loading skeleton
- Data table: column sorting, client-side filtering hook, pagination, sticky header, CSV export
- Number formatting centralized (thousands separators, compact units, currency vs percent)
- Empty and overflow states verified with long labels and 0 rows
- Unit tests for sorting and formatting edge cases

Server-side pagination wiring is done per view in 4.4/4.5.

tasks.name: 3.6 Add spike detection thresholds for error and latency anomalies
tasks.details:
Flag when error rate or latency departs from its normal range so the dashboard can highlight it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Baseline computed per service on a rolling window (e.g. same hour on prior days)
- Flag raised when a metric exceeds N standard deviations or an absolute floor, whichever is higher
- Anomalies stored with window, severity, and the contributing metric
- Backtesting run against one week of real logs, with false-positive rate documented
- Alert noise reviewed with the on-call engineer before enabling notifications

Machine-learning approaches are explicitly out of scope; a documented statistical rule is sufficient for v1.

tasks.name: 4.4 Build customer analytics views (segments, growth, retention)
tasks.details:
Compose the customer-facing pages from the primitives and the customer metrics API.

Acceptance criteria:
- Customer overview page: KPI cards for total/active/new customers, growth chart, segment breakdown
- Segment detail drill-down from the overview
- Every widget states its data freshness (as-of timestamp from the last successful CSV load)
- Widgets degrade independently, so one failed query does not blank the page
- Page verified against a known staging dataset with hand-checked totals

New derived metrics discovered mid-build get scoped as follow-up tasks rather than expanding this one.

tasks.name: 4.5 Build log analytics views (error timeline, latency, top errors)
tasks.details:
Compose the engineering troubleshooting pages from the log metrics API.

Acceptance criteria:
- Error timeline chart with service breakdown and anomaly markers from 3.6
- Latency percentile chart (p50/p95/p99) with service/endpoint selection
- Top error signatures table that expands into a sample stack trace
- Click-through from a chart point into a filtered event list
- Empty-range and no-data-for-service states handled with guidance text

Live log tailing/streaming is out of scope for v1 and would be a separate task.

tasks.name: 4.6 Implement global filters with shared state and URL sync
tasks.details:
One filter bar that drives every widget on a page and survives a page reload or shared link.

Acceptance criteria:
- Date range, customer segment, and service filters available where relevant
- Filter state encoded in the URL; opening a shared link restores the exact view
- Changing a filter refetches only affected widgets, with previous data dimmed rather than cleared
- Invalid or expired filter values fall back to defaults with a visible notice
- Filter behavior consistent between customer and log sections

Cross-page filter persistence beyond the URL is not required for v1.

tasks.name: 4.7 Add loading, empty, error states and accessibility pass
tasks.details:
Make every widget trustworthy when data is slow, missing, or broken, and usable without a mouse.

Acceptance criteria:
- Skeleton loaders for each widget shape; no layout jump on load
- Distinct empty states for "no data yet" vs "no results for these filters"
- Error state per widget with a retry action and a correlation id for support
- Charts expose text/table alternatives and keyboard focus; color contrast meets WCAG AA
- Screen-reader pass on the two core journeys with issues logged and fixed

A full external accessibility audit is a separate engagement and not part of this task.

tasks.name: 5.1 Wire end-to-end integration and smoke suite
tasks.details:
Prove CSV and log data flows reach the dashboard UI in staging.

Acceptance criteria:
- Seeded CSV fixture runs through the pipeline and its numbers appear on the customer page
- Seeded log fixture runs through parsing and aggregation and appears on the log page
- Automated smoke suite exercises upload -> process -> query -> render on every deploy
- Failures report the failing stage (ingest, transform, load, API, UI) in the output
- Suite runs in under 15 minutes against staging

Broader functional coverage is task 5.2; this task is the wiring plus the critical path.

tasks.name: 5.2 Harden unit and integration test coverage with CI gates
tasks.details:
Raise confidence in the parser, transform, aggregation, and API layers, and enforce it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Coverage threshold agreed and enforced in CI for parser/transform modules and API handlers
- Integration tests cover the failure paths: bad encoding, reject-threshold breach, dead-letter lines, inverted time range
- Flaky tests identified and either fixed or quarantined with an owner
- Test data builders exist so new cases do not require hand-editing fixtures
- CI runtime stays under the agreed budget (target 15 minutes)

Chasing 100% coverage is explicitly not a goal; critical-path coverage is.

tasks.name: 5.3 Add pipeline data-quality assertions
tasks.details:
Catch silent data corruption before it reaches a dashboard widget.

Acceptance criteria:
- Assertions per pipeline run: row-count reconciliation, null-rate ceilings on key fields, uniqueness on customer id, freshness SLA
- Aggregates checked against source counts within a stated tolerance
- Failed assertions block the load or flag the dataset as degraded, per an agreed severity policy
- Results surfaced in the run-history view from 2.7
- Each assertion has a named owner and a documented remediation step

Building a full data-observability platform is out of scope; these are targeted assertions.

tasks.name: 5.4 Run load tests and tune dashboard-critical queries
tasks.details:
Confirm the dashboard meets its response-time targets at expected concurrency.

Acceptance criteria:
- Load script simulating the agreed concurrency (default 50 concurrent users) on the two core journeys
- Targets: dashboard page p95 under 3s, API p95 under 800ms on a 7-day range
- Slow queries identified from query logs and optimized (indexes, pre-aggregation, or caching)
- Results recorded with dataset size and concurrency so they can be repeated
- Documented capacity limit and the first bottleneck expected as usage grows

Scaling beyond the pilot user group is a follow-up decision, not a deliverable here.

tasks.name: 5.5 Implement auth, role-based access, and PII review
tasks.details:
Control who sees customer data and logs, and remove sensitive data from places it should not be.

Acceptance criteria:
- SSO login enforced; two roles (business viewer, engineering viewer) with server-side enforcement, not just hidden UI
- Secrets retrieved from the secret manager at runtime; no credentials in code, config, or CI logs
- PII inventory for customer fields and log payloads, with masking applied in log messages where needed
- Data-retention settings reviewed against policy for both CSVs and logs
- Access-review checklist signed off before pilot launch

Penetration testing is not in scope for this milestone revision.

tasks.name: 5.6 Set up monitoring, alerting, and operations runbooks
tasks.details:
Make the platform operable by someone who did not build it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Service health dashboards for pipeline, API, and dashboard (latency, error rate, freshness)
- Alerts routed to the on-call channel with severity levels and no duplicate noisy pages
- Runbooks for: failed CSV run, stuck log ingestion, stale dashboard data, and API outage
- Each runbook lists symptoms, first checks, mitigation, and escalation
- On-call handover walkthrough completed and recorded

Tooling choice should reuse what the team already operates where possible.

tasks.name: 5.7 Execute phased pilot rollout and launch checklist
tasks.details:
Ship to the pilot group in controlled stages with a tested rollback.

Acceptance criteria:
- Launch checklist signed: smoke suite green, load targets met, security sign-off, runbooks published
- Rollout in two stages: internal team for 3 days, then pilot user group
- Rollback procedure tested in staging and documented with a named decision owner
- Feedback channel live and first-week check-in scheduled
- Post-launch monitoring period defined (default 1 week) with explicit success measures

Full general-availability rollout is a separate decision after the pilot review.
